## Occurrence excess of loss {#sec-recipe-reinsurance-occurrence-xol}

You have a two-layer per-occurrence excess programme with partial placements,
and you want the *net* aggregate -- with gross and ceded still visible, so you
can see where the cession went instead of taking the net on faith.

```{python}
a = build('''agg OccurrenceXOL
  15 claims
  10000 xs 0
  sev lognorm 1500 cv 1
  occurrence net of
    50% so 2500 xs 2500 and
    90% so 5000 xs 5000
  mixed gamma 0.25''')
qd(a.reins_summary_df)
```

`occurrence net of ...` applies the programme claim by claim, before the
frequency convolution -- which is what "per occurrence" means and why it cannot
be done by adjusting the aggregate afterwards.

`50% so 2500 xs 2500` cedes half of the 2500-excess-2500 layer, `90% so 5000 xs
5000` nine tenths of the layer above it; `and` chains them into one programme.

Note the program above is the **canonical** form. Partial placements can be
written `so` (*share of*) or `po` (*part of*) and with a percentage or an
absolute amount; all of them normalise to the `<pct>% so <limit> xs <attach>`
spelling you see here, which is why what you wrote and what the library shows
back can differ without anything having changed.

`reins_summary_df` is the exhibit that matters here: three stages (gross,
ceded, net) x three components (freq, sev, agg), with theoretic `EX` next to
the FFT `Est EX`. The frequency row is identical across the three views --
occurrence cover changes what each claim costs, never how many there are.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The check"}

```{python}
# net + ceded = gross, on both severity and aggregate, to grid accuracy
est = a.reins_summary_df['Est EX'].xs('occ')
for component in ('sev', 'agg'):
    gross = est[('gross', component)]
    net = est[('net', component)]
    ceded = est[('ceded', component)]
    assert abs(net + ceded - gross) < 1e-6 * gross
# occurrence cover leaves the claim COUNT alone. Read this off the theoretic
# EX column: the gross frequency has no separate FFT estimate (Est EX is NaN
# there -- there is nothing to estimate, the count is an input).
ex = a.reins_summary_df['EX'].xs('occ')
assert abs(ex[('net', 'freq')] - ex[('gross', 'freq')]) < 1e-9
assert abs(ex[('ceded', 'freq')] - ex[('gross', 'freq')]) < 1e-9
```

:::
